items.q: Which statement about service providers and service consumers is CORRECT?
o: An organization can act as a service provider and a service consumer at the same time
An organization is either a provider or a consumer, never both
Only external companies can be service providers
Service consumers never contribute to value creation
items.x: Organizations form chains of service relationships. For example, an IT department consumes cloud services and provides services to the business, and the business provides services to its own customers.

items.q: A person chooses a personal mobile phone plan, pays for it and uses it. Which roles is this person performing?
items.x: One person can hold several consumer roles. They define the requirements (customer), authorize the spending (sponsor) and use the service (user).

items.q: Which statement BEST describes goods in a service offering?
o: Access to the provider's resources under agreed terms
Physical items whose ownership is transferred to the consumer, who becomes responsible for their future use
Activities the provider performs to address a consumer's needs
Functionality offered to meet a need
items.x: Goods are supplied with ownership transferred to the consumer. Access to resources keeps ownership with the provider, and service actions are activities performed by the provider.

items.q: A mobile plan includes a handset that the customer keeps, unlimited use of the mobile network, and 24/7 technical support. Which element is ACCESS TO RESOURCES?
o: The use of the mobile network
items.x: Using the provider's network is access to resources, because ownership stays with the provider. The handset is goods and technical support is a service action.

items.q: A development team works on a new customer feature. Which of the following is an OUTPUT of the team's work?
o: The new feature is deployed and available in the app
items.x: An output is a deliverable of an activity, in this case the deployed feature. Faster purchases, higher satisfaction and market share are outcomes or results that the outputs help to enable.

items.q: What is a cost?
o: The amount of money spent on a specific activity or resource
The value perceived by a consumer
A possible event that could cause harm
The price paid by a consumer only
items.x: Cost is the amount of money spent on a specific activity or resource. From the consumer's point of view, services remove some costs and impose others.

items.q: Which statement about risk in ITIL is CORRECT?
o: Risk only refers to negative events
Services always remove all risks from consumers
Consumers have no role in managing service risks
Risk can also be defined as uncertainty of outcome, and can relate to positive as well as negative outcomes
items.x: Besides harmful events, ITIL notes that risk can be defined as uncertainty of outcome, which can include positive outcomes. Services remove some risks, impose others, and consumers help to reduce them.

items.q:
Which two of the following are typical aspects of WARRANTY?
1. Availability
2. Report formats
3. Security
4. Screen layouts
items.x: Warranty covers how a product or service performs, including availability, capacity, security and continuity. Report formats and screen layouts relate to functionality, which is utility.

items.q: The root cause of repeated application crashes has been analysed and a workaround documented, but no permanent fix exists yet. How should this be classified?
items.x: A known error is a problem that has been analysed and has not been resolved. Documenting the workaround helps the service desk restore service quickly until a permanent solution is justified and implemented.

items.q: A user asks the service desk for access to the marketing team's shared folder. How should this be classified?
items.x: Requests for access are pre-defined service actions that are a normal part of service delivery, so they are service requests. Nothing is broken, so it is not an incident.

items.q: ITIL (Version 5) places strong emphasis on 'digital product and service management'. What does this mean?
o: Managing only the IT infrastructure that runs services
Managing digital products and services together across their whole lifecycle, from discovery to support
Replacing service management with project management
Managing only products that are sold to external customers
items.x: Version 5 brings product management and service management together. Digital products and services are managed as one across the lifecycle, from discovering needs through to operation, delivery and support.

items.q: A company chooses a hosting provider powered by renewable energy that also has ethical labour practices in its supply chain. Which aspect of quality is MOST directly being considered?
items.x: Sustainability considers the environmental, social and economic impact of products and services, for example energy sources and ethical supply chains.

items.q: Relationships with other organizations can range from formal contracts with a clear separation of responsibilities to flexible partnerships with shared goals and risks. Which dimension describes these relationships?
items.x: The partners and suppliers dimension covers the organization's relationships with other organizations involved in creating, delivering and supporting products and services, and the agreements that govern them.

items.q: An online retailer has huge sales peaks in November and uses on-demand cloud capacity from a supplier to handle them. Which factor influencing supplier strategy does this illustrate?
items.x: Seasonal or highly variable demand makes flexible supplier services, such as on-demand cloud capacity, attractive. This is the demand patterns factor.

items.q: Staff are afraid to report their mistakes because people have been blamed in the past, so problems stay hidden. Which dimension needs the MOST attention?
items.x: Culture is part of the organizations and people dimension. A culture of trust and transparency encourages people to raise issues and suggest improvements without fear.

items.q: Rising inflation and exchange-rate changes increase the cost of the cloud services an organization buys. Under PESTLE, which type of external factor is this?
items.x: Inflation, exchange rates, budgets and economic cycles are Economic factors. They influence all four dimensions.

items.q: An organization has purchased a SaaS product and is now configuring it and testing its integrations before it goes live. Which lifecycle activity is MAINLY being performed?
items.x: Build creates, configures and tests the solution, including configuring and integrating acquired components. Acquire was the earlier decision to obtain the SaaS product.

items.q: A team builds a business case and confirms which customer needs are worth pursuing before any design work starts. Which lifecycle activity is this?
items.x: Discover explores needs, demand and opportunities and aligns them with strategy before resources are committed. Design follows once needs are validated.

items.q: Which statement about the relationship between management practices and lifecycle activities is CORRECT?
o: Each practice belongs to exactly one lifecycle activity
Practices are used only in the Operate activity
Lifecycle activities do not use practices
A practice can contribute to several lifecycle activities
items.x: Practices provide capabilities that are used wherever they are needed. For example, supplier management contributes to Acquire, Transition, Operate and Support.

items.q: What is the main focus of the Transition activity?
o: Moving new or changed products and services into the live environment
items.x: Transition moves new or changed products and services, such as releases, into the live environment in a controlled way, along with the related changes and arrangements.

items.q: Which statement about value is part of the 'focus on value' principle?
o: Value is fixed once a service is designed
Value can change over time and in different circumstances, so it must be revisited
Only the provider can define value
Value applies only to customers who pay
items.x: Consumers' needs and perceptions change, so the organization must keep checking what value means to them. Value also matters to other stakeholders, not only to paying customers.

items.q: When assessing the current state, which starting point does 'start where you are' recommend?
o: The opinions of the most senior manager
The capabilities of the latest tools on the market
The structure of the IT department
The customer or the desired outcome
items.x: 'Look at what exists as objectively as possible, using the customer or desired outcome as the starting point' is a key recommendation for applying 'start where you are'.

items.q: 'The ecosystem is constantly changing, so feedback is essential' is guidance for applying which guiding principle?
items.x: Because circumstances change, iterations must be checked against feedback before, during and after the work, so that the effort stays focused on value.

items.q: A problem manager invites service desk agents to root cause analysis workshops because they know how users experience the issue. Which guiding principle does this MOST directly illustrate?
items.x: Working with the right people in the right roles produces better results and greater buy-in. Collaboration across team boundaries is the core of this principle.

items.q: When designing a new product, a team considers people, information and technology, suppliers and value streams together, along with how the product interacts with existing services. Which guiding principle is this?
items.x: Considering all four dimensions and the interactions with other products and services is the essence of 'think and work holistically'.

items.q: A weekly two-hour status meeting that adds little value is replaced by a short dashboard update. Which recommendation of 'keep it simple and practical' does this reflect?
o: Comprehend the whole, but do something
Respect the time of the people involved
Use the customer as the starting point
items.x: Processes and activities that consume people's time without adding value should be simplified or removed. Respecting people's time increases engagement and efficiency.

items.q: After the password reset process has been simplified, an AI assistant is introduced to perform resets without human involvement. Which guiding principle is being applied?
items.x: The process was first optimized and then automated, so technology handles repetitive work and people focus on activities where they add value.

items.q: In a large company, who typically acts as the governing body?
items.x: The governing body is accountable at the highest level for the organization's performance and compliance. In a company this is typically the board of directors.

items.q: Through the 'direct' activity, to whom can the policies set by the governing body apply?
o: Only to the governing body itself
Across the organization and, where relevant, to its suppliers, partners and other stakeholders
items.x: Policies set requirements for behaviour across the organization and, where relevant, its suppliers, partners and other stakeholders. Strategies set direction and priorities.

items.q: Where does continual improvement appear in ITIL?
o: Only as a one-off project when performance is poor
As a component of the value system and as a management practice, applied at all levels of the organization
Only in the responsibilities of the governing body
items.x: Continual improvement is a recurring activity at every level. It is a component of the value system and also one of the general management practices.

items.q: To what scope can the continual improvement model be applied?
o: To any level, from the whole organization to a single product, practice or team
items.x: The model is a high-level, iterative guide that can be applied to improvements of any size and scope, from organization-wide transformations to a single team's working practices.

items.q: The step 'Did we get there?' shows that the improvement targets were NOT achieved. What should happen next?
o: The initiative should be closed and forgotten
The targets should be changed so that they appear to be met
The organization should analyse why, and return to earlier steps of the model to adjust its approach
The governing body should replace the team
items.x: If targets are missed, the organization learns why and iterates through the model again, for example by revising the plan, instead of declaring success or abandoning the improvement.

items.q: What happened to the ITIL 4 technical management practices in ITIL (Version 5)?
o: They were deleted and are no longer part of ITIL
They became a third lifecycle model
The separate technical management group was removed and its practices were placed in the remaining two groups, keeping 34 practices in total
items.x: Version 5 has two practice groups: general management and product and service management. The former technical management practices, such as deployment management, were redistributed, so the total stays at 34.

items.q: What is the purpose of the service level management practice?
o: To capture demand for incident resolution
To set clear business-based targets for service levels, and to ensure that delivery of services is properly assessed, monitored and managed against these targets
To manage the full lifecycle of IT assets
items.x: Service level management agrees business-based targets and manages delivery against them. Good agreements relate to outcomes and experience, not only to technical metrics.

items.q: Which list contains ONLY components of the ITIL value system?
o: Four dimensions, service desk, CMDB, practices
Guiding principles, governance, management practices, continual improvement
items.x: The value system includes the guiding principles, governance, the activities that turn demand into value, management practices and continual improvement. The four dimensions apply to the value system but are not one of its components.

items.q: Which statement about opportunity and demand is CORRECT?
o: They trigger activities in the value system, but not every opportunity has to be pursued, so they must be prioritized
Every opportunity must be acted upon immediately
Demand is only created by external customers
Opportunity and demand are outputs of the value system
items.x: Opportunity and demand are inputs that trigger activities. Organizations prioritize them, because resources are limited and not every opportunity creates enough value.

items.q: Which sequence BEST describes the typical steps of value stream mapping and improvement?
o: Design the future state, then automate, then identify the value stream
Identify the value stream, map the current state, analyse it for waste and bottlenecks, design the future state, plan the improvements
Buy a tool, map the organization chart, write procedures
Analyse the future state, map the past state, close the value stream
items.x: Mapping starts by identifying the value stream and mapping its current state. The team then analyses it, designs an improved future state and plans the improvement work, usually iteratively.

items.q: In a value stream, work is actively done for 4 hours in total, but the lead time from request to delivery is 40 hours. What is the flow efficiency?
items.x: Flow efficiency is process time divided by lead time: 4 / 40 = 10%. The work spends 90% of its time waiting, which shows where improvement effort should go.

items.q: In the ITIL AI Capability Model, which capability is MOST concerned with selecting, organizing and maintaining data, content and knowledge so that it stays accurate and relevant?
items.x: Curation is about organizing and maintaining data, content and knowledge, for example keeping knowledge articles and a service catalogue accurate. Creation generates new content, and coordination orchestrates tasks and workflows.

items.q: How does Agile relate to ITIL?
o: Agile's iterative, incremental delivery with frequent feedback is consistent with ITIL principles such as 'progress iteratively with feedback'
Agile and ITIL cannot be used in the same organization
Agile is a standard against which organizations are certified
Agile replaces the ITIL value system
items.x: ITIL is designed to work with Agile. Agile emphasizes small iterations, collaboration and feedback, which match several ITIL guiding principles.
